ctx: Acts 17 follows Paul and Silas across Macedonia. In Thessalonica Paul spent
, and trouble sent them away by night. Berea is the next stop.

When Luke writes 'the Scriptures' here, he means the Law, the Prophets and the Writings: the books Paul could open in a synagogue. The New Testament did not yet exist. The only standard on the table was the Old Testament, and Paul argued from it,

ctx.q: opening and setting forth that it was necessary for the Christ to have suffered and to have risen out from the dead

inv: Luke pays the Bereans a compliment no church leader hands out lightly:

inv.q: more noble than those in Thessalonica

inv: . The reason follows at once, in two parts. They

inv.q: received the word with all readiness

inv: , so they were not hostile. And they were

inv.q: every day examining the Scriptures, if these things were so

inv: , so they were not gullible. Readiness and examination, together. Take either away and the nobility goes with it.

Look at what the examining was aimed at. Not a doubt about Scripture, but a question put to Paul: were these things so? The Bereans treated an apostle's message as a claim that Scripture could confirm or fail to confirm. That is Deuteronomy 19:15 in the hands of ordinary listeners. Scripture was the second witness, and they went looking for it daily. Paul had made that possible: his own method was to reason from the text, not to demand trust in his office.
. The checking did not drive them away from faith. It led them into it, on ground they had verified for themselves.
That habit is the one this series asks of you: a passage a day, the text open, and the question put to each claim, ours included. Is it so?

w: Paul's own method in the city before Berea: reasoning from the Scriptures, so his message could be checked there.
x.q: he reasoned with them from the Scriptures

w: Paul's letter to the church he had just left states the Bereans' habit as a command.
x.q: test all things. Hold fast to the good

w: John gives the same discipline as a rule for spirits and prophets.
x.q: do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits

w: Christ had already taught that the Scriptures speak of him, which is what Paul was reasoning from.
x.q: He interpreted to them the things concerning Himself in all the Scriptures

take: The New Testament praises listeners who checked an apostle against the Scriptures. Readiness and examination belong together.
